title: 20-Year Treasury Bond auction (December first reopening) — the latest December 20-Year on record, selling into Christmas week
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Auction-Schedule.pdf), fetched direct by plain curl 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes) by the treasury-20y-bond-2027-01-20 initial research, text layer decompressed stream-by-stream and re-tokenised. Read verbatim from that text: `20-Year  BONDR` (the trailing `R` is Treasury's reopening marker) announced `Thursday, December 17, 2026`, auctioned `Wednesday, December 23, 2026`, settled `Monday, December 28, 2026`. The 1:00 p.m. ET bidding deadline is NOT taken from the schedule — it is fiscaldata `auctions_query`'s `closing_time_comp`, which reads `01:00 PM` on every 20-Year auction since 2020-05 (n=77, same-day pull). Filed estimate on the two limits this lane records: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep
notes: DISCOVERED during the treasury-20y-bond-2027-01-20 never-assessed initial research (2026-09-09). PROPOSED BECAUSE IT IS THE DIRECT PREDECESSOR PRINT of the CUSIP the proposer sells, and the calendar already tracks the other three legs of that cycle (treasury-20y-bond-2026-11-18 new issue, this first reopening, treasury-20y-bond-2027-01-20 second reopening) — tracking two of three leaves the January sale with no baseline. WHAT MAKES IT WORTH ITS OWN LEDGER RATHER THAN A LINE IN THE PROPOSER'S: 2026-12-23 is LATER THAN ANY DECEMBER 20-YEAR AUCTION ON RECORD. Every prior December 20-Year fell between the 17th and the 21st — 2020-12-21, 2021-12-21, 2022-12-21, 2023-12-20, 2024-12-17, 2025-12-17 (fiscaldata auctions_query, original_security_term 20-Year, 2020-05 onward, n=77, pulled 2026-09-09). This one bids the day before the christmas-eve-half-day-2026-12-24 session, in the thinnest dealer-balance-sheet week of the year, alongside pce-2026-12-23 (high), gdp-q3-2026-third-2026-12-23 and durable-goods-2026-12-23 at 8:30 ET. CONSEQUENCE THE PROPOSER RECORDS: whatever this sale prints is a poor baseline for 2027-01-20 and must not be read as the cycle's demand level. SIZE EXPECTATION $13B on a 24-of-24 reopening base rate, published in the 2026-11-04 refunding statement and read back at the 2026-12-17 announcement — owned by the announcement lane, not by this proposal. GRADING NOTE FOR WHOEVER RESEARCHES IT, from the proposer's own measurement: at a fixed $13B offering, bid-to-cover, gross tendered dollars, dealer take and the high-minus-median yield dispersion are one statistic (r=0.999 / -0.849 / -0.769 against bid-to-cover, n=24); only the indirect/direct split is close to orthogonal. Proposed as an estimate; `symbols: []` and no house playbook is rates-keyed, so nothing here licenses an entry.
